onboarding.supportGithubBody: We're open source and committed to providing a free terminal for individual users. Please show your support by giving us a star on
onboarding.communityBody: Get help, submit feature requests, report bugs, or just chat with fellow terminal enthusiasts.
onboarding.privacyBody: Anonymous usage data helps us improve features you use.
onboarding.telemetryDisabledLead: No problem, we respect your privacy.
onboarding.telemetryDisabledBody: But, without usage data, we're flying blind. A GitHub star helps us know Wave is useful and worth maintaining.
onboarding.waveAIBody: Wave AI is your terminal assistant with context. I can read your terminal output, analyze widgets, read/write files, and help you solve problems faster.
onboarding.waveAIToggleButton: Toggle the Wave AI panel with the
onboarding.waveAIShortcut: Or use the keyboard shortcut {{shortcut}} to quickly toggle
onboarding.waveAIProviders: Bring your own API keys or run local models with Ollama, LM Studio, and other OpenAI-compatible providers
onboarding.durableLead: Close your laptop, switch networks, restart Wave — your remote sessions keep running.
onboarding.durableState: Shell state, running programs, and terminal history are all preserved
onboarding.durableReconnect: Sessions automatically reconnect when your connection is restored
onboarding.durableBuffer: Buffered output streams back in, never miss a line
onboarding.durableSummary: All the persistence of tmux, built into your terminal. Look for the shield icon to enable durability on any SSH session.
onboarding.magnifyLead: Magnify any block to focus on what matters. Expand terminals, editors, and previews for a better view.
onboarding.magnifyEfficiency: Use the magnify feature to work with complex outputs and large files more efficiently.
onboarding.magnifyHeaderIcon: You can also magnify a block by clicking on the

onboarding.filesLead: Wave can preview markdown, images, and video files on both local and remote machines.
onboarding.filesViewSuffix: to preview files in Wave's graphical viewer
onboarding.filesEditSuffix: to open config files or code files in Wave's graphical editor
onboarding.filesSummary: These commands work seamlessly on both local and remote machines, making it easy to view and edit files wherever they are.

minor.waveAiLead: Wave AI is your terminal assistant with full context. It can read your terminal output, analyze widgets, read and write files, and help you solve problems faster.
minor.newInV013Body: Wave AI now supports local models and bring-your-own-key! Use Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, OpenRouter, or any OpenAI-compatible provider.
minor.newInV014Body: Durable SSH sessions survive network drops, laptop sleep, and restarts, all without tmux or screen.
minor.thanksTitle: Thanks for being an early Wave adopter! ⭐
minor.thanksBody: A GitHub star shows your support for Wave (and open-source) and helps us reach more developers.

v0121.lead: Patch release focused on shell integration improvements, Wave AI enhancements, and restoring syntax highlighting in code editor blocks.

shell.title: Shell Integration & Context
shell.item1Body: Wave now automatically tracks and restores your current directory across restarts for bash, zsh, fish, and pwsh shells.
shell.item2Body: Tracks when your shell is ready, last command executed, and exit codes for better terminal management.

ai.title: Wave AI Improvements
ai.item1: Display reasoning summaries while waiting for AI responses.
ai.item2: Enhanced terminal context: AI now has access to shell state, current directory, command history, and exit codes.
ai.item3: Added feedback buttons (thumbs up/down) for AI responses.
ai.item4: Added copy button to easily copy AI responses to clipboard.

other.title: Other Changes
other.item1: Mobile user agent emulation support for web widgets.
other.item2: Fixed padding for header buttons in code editor.
other.item3: Restored syntax highlighting in code editor preview blocks.

v0122.lead: Wave AI can now create and modify files with visual diff previews and easy rollback capabilities. Plus performance improvements and bug fixes.

fileEditing.title: Wave AI File Editing
fileEditing.item1Body: Wave AI can now create and modify files with your approval.
fileEditing.item2Body: See exactly what will change before approving edits.
fileEditing.item3Body: Revert file changes with a simple "Revert File" button.

ai.title: Additional AI Improvements
ai.item1: Drag and drop files from preview viewer directly to Wave AI.
ai.item3: Adjustable thinking level and max output tokens per chat.
ai.item4: Improved tool descriptions and input validations.

bugfix.title: Bug Fixes & Improvements
bugfix.item1: Fixed significant memory leak in the RPC system.

v0123.lead: Wave AI model upgrade to GPT-5.1, new secret management features, and improved terminal input handling for interactive CLI tools.

ai.title: Wave AI Updates
ai.item1Body: Upgraded to OpenAI's GPT-5.1 model for improved responses.
ai.item2Body: New dropdown to select between Quick, Balanced, and Deep thinking modes.
ai.item3: Fixed path mismatch issue when restoring AI write file backups.

terminal.title: Terminal Improvements
terminal.item1Body: Better support for CLI tools like Claude Code.
terminal.item2Body: Paste images directly into terminal (saved to temp files).
terminal.item3: Shift+Enter now inserts newlines by default for multi-line commands.
terminal.item4: Fixed duplicate text issue when switching input methods (IME).

secret.title: Secret Store
secret.item1Body: Store and manage sensitive credentials securely.

v0130.lead: Wave v0.13 brings local AI support, bring-your-own-key (BYOK), a redesigned configuration system, and improved terminal functionality.

ai.title: Local AI & BYOK
ai.item1Body: Connect to Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, OpenRouter, and other local or hosted models.
ai.item3Body: Built-in configs for OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Azure, and custom endpoints.
ai.item4Body: Easily switch between models and providers.

config.title: Configuration Widget
config.item1Body: Dedicated widget accessible from the sidebar.
config.item2Body: Browse and edit settings with improved validation and error handling.
config.item3Body: Manage API keys and credentials from the config widget.

terminal.title: Terminal Updates
terminal.item1Body: Enabled by default for better multi-line paste behavior.
terminal.item2Body: Ctrl+V now works as standard paste on Windows.
terminal.item3Body: Store SSH passwords in Wave's secret store.

v0131.lead: Wave v0.13.1 focuses on Windows platform improvements, Wave AI visual updates, and enhanced terminal navigation.

windows.title: Windows Platform Enhancements
windows.item1Body: Cleaner interface with controls integrated into the tab-bar header.
windows.item3Body: Improved SSH agent support on Windows.
windows.item4Body: Wave AI focus key changed to Alt:0 on Windows.

ai.title: Wave AI Updates
ai.item1Body: Complete UI refresh with transparency support for custom backgrounds.
ai.item2Body: Wave AI now works with bring-your-own-key and local models without requiring telemetry.

terminal.title: Terminal Improvements
terminal.item1Body: Added Shift+Home, Shift+End, Shift+PageUp, and Shift+PageDown for better navigation.

v0140.lead: Wave v0.14 introduces Durable Sessions. Enable them to keep your remote sessions alive through network interruptions, computer sleep, and restarts. They will automatically reconnect when your connection is restored.

durable.title: Durable SSH Sessions
durable.item1Body: Programs and shell state survive disconnects.

ai.title: Wave AI Updates
ai.item2Body: Ability to stop AI responses mid-generation.

terminal.title: Terminal Improvements
terminal.item1Body: Quick access to splits, themes, and more.
terminal.item2Body: CLI apps can copy to system clipboard.

tabBar.configCleanBody: There are no longer any errors detected in your config.

standard.title: Standard SSH Session
standard.body: Standard SSH sessions end when the connection drops. Durable sessions keep your shell state, running programs, and history alive through network changes, computer sleep, and Wave restarts.

attached.title: Durable Session (Attached)
attached.body: Your shell state, running programs, and history are protected. This session will survive network disconnects.

detached.title: Durable Session (Detached)
detached.body: Connection lost, but your session is still running on the remote server. Wave will automatically reconnect when the connection is restored.

awaitingConnection.title: Durable Session (Awaiting Connection)
awaitingConnection.body: Configured for a durable session. The session will start when the connection is established.

awaitingStart.title: Durable Session (Awaiting Start)
awaitingStart.body: Configured for a durable session, but session hasn't started yet. Click below to start it manually.

ended.title: Durable Session (Ended)
ended.body: The durable session has ended. This block is still configured for durable sessions.

exited.title: Durable Session (Ended, Exited)
exited.body: The shell was terminated and is no longer running. This block is still configured for durable sessions.

lost.title: Durable Session (Ended, Lost)
lost.body: The session was lost or not found on the remote server. This may have occurred due to a system reboot or the session being manually terminated.

failed.title: Durable Session (Failed to Start)
failed.body: The durable session failed to start.
